comment: Authoritative byte-level vectors for the payloads this gateway authors: the /ws/provider and /ws/kyok handshake. The gateway's, souk-agent-sdk's and souk-client-sdk's test suites all consume this file, so the three restatements of the handshake cannot drift from each other; an external implementation in any language replays it: build each payload from `inputs`, assert the exact `payload_utf8` bytes, and check `signature_hex` verifies (deterministic Ed25519 — reproducing it is equivalent) under the published key for that side. The signing-payload families souk core authors (souk-register, souk-register-llm, souk-delete-agent, souk-kyok-call) are published upstream in AgentSouk/docs/contract-vectors.json under the same provider test key. Both test keys are for vectors only — never accept either in a real deployment.

provider_test_key.comment: The same test key upstream's contract-vectors.json publishes, so one keypair drives both files.

souk_test_key.comment: The souk side of the mutual handshake signs too — that is the point of it.

inputs.note: the digest is over the exact hello text as it went on the wire, never a re-serialization; the same payload shape serves /ws/kyok, whose hello carries modelNames instead of agentNames

frames.comment: The frame vocabulary each socket accepts inbound after the handshake. The gateway's dispatch is asserted against these sets, so a type added in code without a row here fails a test. Full field semantics live in docs/server-mode.md.
